flashcard_questions.q: Which colder, more sinister noun does Dickens use to name the third spirit?
How does the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come communicate with Scrooge?
flashcard_questions.a: Only by pointing — it never speaks a single word.

flashcard_questions.q: What effect does the third spirit's silence have on Scrooge and the reader?
flashcard_questions.a: It forces them to interpret the visions for themselves, making the experience more intense.

flashcard_questions.q: Which quotation shows Scrooge admitting his terror of the final spirit?
flashcard_questions.a: “I fear you more than any spectre I have seen.”

flashcard_questions.q: Which word means a genre combining horror, the supernatural and dark atmospheric settings?
What condition do the businessmen attach to attending the dead man's funeral?
flashcard_questions.a: They will go only “if lunch is provided”.

flashcard_questions.q: Which devil's nickname do the businessmen give the dead man?
What dramatic irony runs through the businessmen scene in Stave 4?
flashcard_questions.a: The reader realises the dead man is Scrooge before Scrooge does.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does Dickens present the thieves in Old Joe's shop sympathetically?
flashcard_questions.a: They are driven to crime by the want that men like Scrooge have perpetuated.

flashcard_questions.q: What is meant by juxtaposition in a novel?
flashcard_questions.a: Placing two things side by side to highlight their differences and create meaning.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Dickens set against Scrooge's unmourned death in Stave 4?
flashcard_questions.a: Tiny Tim's death, mourned by a poor family united in love.

flashcard_questions.q: Which earlier warning does Tiny Tim's death fulfil?
flashcard_questions.a: “I see a vacant seat… and a crutch without an owner.”

flashcard_questions.q: How does Peter measure his father's grief after Tiny Tim dies?
flashcard_questions.a: Bob now walks “a little slower than he used”.

flashcard_questions.q: Which quotation describes the neglected churchyard holding Scrooge's grave?
flashcard_questions.a: “overrun by grass and weeds, the growth of vegetation's death, not life”

flashcard_questions.q: What pledge does Scrooge make at his own gravestone?
flashcard_questions.a: “I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.”

notes: 15 cards: 7 theme or character to quotation, 4 quotation-to-effect, 2 term-to-definition (Gothic as 'Which word means…', juxtaposition), 1 structure card (the silence), 1 context card (Old Joe's thieves and Want). Rewrote the Old Joe scene as a cause card rather than listing the three thieves, which would have been an enumerated answer. Dropped 'want', 'redemption', 'indifference' and 'allegorical' as glossary cards — they are tested through the quotation cards or are too generic to retrieve uniquely.
